messages.subject: Probabilistic Inference
messages.body_plain:
Hello; Dear all,

I'm doing some work on evaluating volcano seismic events by post-evaluation
using Bayesian Networks. I'm quite new to Bayesian Networks and I chose to
work with deal.

I went through the tutorials rats, ksl, reinis and simulation, as I read
the article "deal: A Package for Learning Bayesian Networks".

It seems to be really easy to find the best network for a given dataset.
But in my case, I would additionally like to do some probabilistic
inference, e.g. given the conditional probabilities, the nodes and arcs of
the specified network, how do the probabilities of this network change if
I observe on variable (set this variable to 100%). Unfortunately I couldn't
find any hint in the deal help pages, nor the mailing list archive nor on
Google how to accomplish this task using deal.  

My question is now, does deal support probabilistic inference and if
so, how do I do this?

If deal does not support probabilistic inference could you recommend me
one of the other free-packages, preferable in R AND running on Linux/Unix,
with which I can do this exercise?

Advanced thanks,
Moritz Beyreuther

messages.subject: Re: Probabilistic Inference
messages.body_plain:
Dear Moritz
 
Thank you for your interest in 'deal'. The package does not have tools for doing probabilistic inference. You may save a 'learned' network as a file in the '.net' format, see help(savenet). This file may be imported into e.g. Hugin (commercial, see www.hugin.com) for doing inference.
 
Best,
Claus
